name: Development Status Report
one_liner: The team's progress, in the Project Status Report's own terms.
purpose: The Development Status Report documents and communicates the status of the A-PCT towards the development goals, and is incorporated at the project reporting level. Like the Project Status Report it carries tracking information on cost, schedule, scope, risks, issues, changes and forecasts for the project's next steps, and it can follow each iteration and/or each release depending on the project's reporting needs. One of its key elements is the burndown chart, at both iteration and release level.

traps: Development Status Report becomes a section of the Project Status Report.
PrOw is only Informed — the Product Owner does not own progress reporting.
Iteration burndown tracks effort; release burndown tracks functionality delivered.
The p.85 phase table says Created in Planning and Created in Executing — not 'Updated'.
The Daily Stand-up is not a status meeting; this report is where status lives.
